criminal_detail: No criminal charges against former officer Kevin Norris have been reported in coverage found. Reporting states he resigned from the department (Deseret News: in March, after illegally accessing information about the plaintiff's family through police databases; the complaint per other coverage says he resigned in 2022). Separately, in October 2024 the plaintiff herself was charged with second-degree felony theft of a rental vehicle and was named a suspect in an August 2024 arson investigation, which she denies; those matters concern the plaintiff, not the accused officer.
incident_date_approx: June 2019 (two alleged assaults); alleged harassment and intimidation of the plaintiff's family from 2019 onward, Saratoga Springs, Utah
description: A woman filed a federal civil rights lawsuit on January 9, 2023 in the U.S. District Court for the District of Utah against the City of Saratoga Springs, former officer Kevin Norris, and city officials including the police chief, assistant police chief, and city manager. The suit alleges that Norris sexually assaulted her twice in June 2019 while meeting with her in his personal truck to discuss a case, and that she and her family were then repeatedly harassed, stalked, threatened, and intimidated, including slashed tires, keyed cars, and windows shot with BB guns. According to the complaint, the police chief, assistant police chief, and city manager dismissed her complaints and requests for help, effectively covering up the alleged attacks, and a department detective who reported his suspicions about Norris was suspended and later fired. The complaint alleges Norris resigned after illegally accessing information about the plaintiff's family through police databases. The suit seeks $4 million in damages for sexual harassment, discrimination, conspiracy, and unlawful seizure; no resolution has been reported in available coverage.
